usageNotes: Use this to modify an existing TFA entry for a user — typically to toggle it enabled/disabled or update its description. A user can edit their own entries; editing another user's entries requires the User.Modify privilege. Note that `allowtoken` is false, so this call must be authenticated with a real user session or ticket, not an API token.

examples.summary: Disable a TOTP entry for a user (e.g. during account recovery)

tips: The `password` field is the current password of the user making the request, not the target user — required when a non-admin user modifies their own TFA entry.
To find a valid TFA entry `id`, first call GET /access/tfa/{userid} to list all entries for the user.
API tokens cannot call this endpoint (`allowtoken: false`); use a user ticket obtained via POST /access/ticket.
